name: Salesforce
blocker: The API needs an edition that includes it (Enterprise or above, or the Professional add-on). Developers can use a free Developer Edition org. Auth must go through an External Client App, since new connected apps are restricted. Public listing of a distributed app needs AppExchange Security Review.

name: Copper
blocker: The API is tier-gated: it is available on trial, Professional and Business plans only. OAuth for multi-customer use requires Copper to register the app by email (partners@copper.com).

name: DealCloud
blocker: No self-serve developer access. Getting credentials needs a DealCloud site, so a developer needs a customer tenant or a sandbox from Intapp. Sandboxes are offered to Intapp clients. Each customer must also have an admin enable the API capability and issue a per-user API key. Whether the API is a separately licensed add-on is unconfirmed.

name: Intercom
blocker: Public multi-customer OAuth apps need Intercom review/approval before other workspaces can install; some API endpoints are restricted by the customer's Intercom plan (403 'API Plan restricted'), with the affected endpoints not identified.

name: Freshdesk
blocker: The API is not available on the Free plan (0 calls/min). Customers need a paid plan (Growth or above) and must supply their own subdomain and API key; there is no OAuth. Developers can use a free trial (50 calls/min).

name: Pylon
blocker: No self-serve signup: a developer needs a sales-assisted trial/demo org (or a paid seat) to get a workspace, and an Admin there must create the API token. Which tier includes the REST API, and whether trial orgs can issue tokens, is unconfirmed.

name: Help Scout
blocker: The Inbox API is not available on the Free plan; customers need a paid plan (Standard or above) and reporting endpoints need Plus or Pro.

name: Gladly
blocker: No self-serve or trial developer access was found. Credentials require an existing Gladly customer org with the API User permission, and a sandbox must be purchased through a Gladly CSM or Support. A customer or Gladly contact is needed to start.

name: Slack
blocker: Developers can build and test for free. A multi-workspace product used commercially needs Slack Marketplace approval to avoid the Tier 1 limit on conversations.history and conversations.replies (1 request/minute, 15 messages), and to use the Slack MCP server.

name: Lark (Larksuite)
blocker: Custom-app API use is tier-gated. Starter-edition tenants get only 10,000 Basic API calls per month, and Advanced APIs need a purchased quota package on a Basic, Pro or Enterprise edition. Store apps are unmetered, but they need ISV qualification and app review.

name: Discord
blocker: Free to build and test. To serve many customers, a public bot must be verified by Discord once it passes 100 servers, and privileged intents such as Message Content need Discord review at 10,000+ users. The bot must also be installed in each customer's guild, and some scopes are partner-only.

name: Aircall
blocker: A multi-tenant OAuth integration needs approval as an Aircall Technology Partner, which Aircall can decline. Aircall issues the sandbox and the OAuth credentials only after approval. Basic Auth keys work now but only for a single customer's own account.

name: Google Ads
blocker: Developer access is free (Test access on enabling the API), but production use needs Google to grant an access tier to the Cloud project. Explorer is only available if Google lets you apply, and it is capped at 2,880 ops/day with no account linking, user management or keyword planning. Real multi-tenant scale needs Standard access, which is a manual audit of about 10 business days. Upgrade rejections have been reported.

name: Meta Ads
blocker: Development works free with a Meta developer app, but a public multi-customer production app needs Business Verification and Meta App Review for advanced access (ads_read/ads_management, and ads_mcp_management for the MCP server) and the Full access tier. Limited tier is heavily rate-limited and for development only.

name: LinkedIn Ads
blocker: Developer access requires LinkedIn to approve an Advertising API application. Managing more than 5 ad accounts needs a separate Standard tier request through a support ticket, and LinkedIn may decline it.

name: Pinterest
blocker: Developers need Pinterest approval of an app request for Trial access, then an upgrade to Standard access to serve real users. Newer apps may also face PINNER_DATA_ACCESS_DENIED limits on non-business users' boards and Pins.

name: Threads (Meta)
blocker: Serving users outside the developer's own app roles requires Meta App Review and publishing of the app, for each permission. Without review, only Threads Testers on the app can authorize it.

name: SendGrid
blocker: The free trial is time-limited (60 days, 100 emails/day, 100 contacts). Free plans are retired, so customers need a paid Email API and/or Marketing Campaigns plan to keep sending after the trial. Sender/domain authentication may also be needed.

name: Shopify
blocker: Each merchant must install via an OAuth app (new apps can't use store-created custom app tokens); public distribution requires App Store review, and protected customer data (customers/orders, incl. name/email/address/phone) requires Shopify approval for public apps.

name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
blocker: No self-serve or free developer route to a B2C Commerce instance. Dev credentials and sandboxes require a licensed tenant and purchased sandbox credits through a Salesforce Account Executive. Each customer's Account Manager admin must then create an API client or SLAS client. No central OAuth app exists.

name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
blocker: Credentials are per merchant. The merchant admin must create an Integration and either use OAuth 1.0a signing or enable the standalone-bearer setting. SaaS needs Adobe IMS/Developer Console setup. Developer access without a licensed Adobe Commerce instance is only confirmed for Magento Open Source.

name: Squarespace
blocker: API keys need the merchant's Commerce Advanced plan, and a public multi-customer OAuth app needs Squarespace to review and approve the OAuth client before credentials are issued.

name: Ecwid
blocker: Customers' stores need a paid Ecwid plan for API access; sources suggest Venture or higher, but this is unconfirmed. Developers can get a free upgrade by emailing Ecwid. Reaching many customers through OAuth means passing App Market verification for a public app.

blocker: The API needs an eligible paid Ahrefs plan, for developers and for customers. Usage draws on a metered API-unit allowance, and free test queries are limited to ahrefs.com/wordcount.com targets.

name: Sherlock
blocker: Sherlock is a local CLI with no hosted API and no credentials. A Composio toolkit would need to run it in a sandbox or container. Whether that execution model is supported is unresolved.

name: Waterfall.io
blocker: API keys are not self-serve; developers must contact the Waterfall team for access and pricing before they can get credentials.

name: Supabase
blocker: Not a hard blocker. Supabase has two API surfaces: the Management API (PAT or OAuth2) and the per-project data API (a project URL plus a secret key). The connection model must pick one or support both. Free-plan projects pause after 1 week of inactivity.

name: Datadog
blocker: Free-tier API access is unconfirmed. OAuth2 is restricted to approved Technology Partners, so general toolkits would rely on API key + application key or PATs.

name: QuickBooks
blocker: Free sandbox and a documented API are available, but production keys need Intuit's app assessment questionnaire and approval plus an annual security review. Under the Intuit App Partner Program, the free Builder tier caps data-read (CorePlus) calls at 500,000 per month and blocks calls above that. Heavier apps need a paid Silver or higher tier.

name: Xero
blocker: The free Starter tier allows only 5 connected organisations. A multi-tenant integration needs a paid tier (Core at $35 AUD/month for 50 connections, Plus for 1,000 connections, which requires App Certification). Each organisation can connect only 5 uncertified apps.

name: Brex
blocker: No sandbox: developers need a real Brex account where an admin accepts the API agreement and creates a token. No OAuth app model was found for the REST API (only for MCP), so each customer admin supplies a token.

name: Ramp
blocker: Credentials require an existing Ramp customer account with admin access, or an approved sandbox request (form-gated). Some endpoints also need specific Ramp plan features, and some scopes are partner-only.

name: PitchBook
blocker: There is no self-serve developer access. The API needs a standalone contract with PitchBook's Direct Data team, an API key from PitchBook, a sandbox key from the account manager, and purchased credits. MCP access also needs a PitchBook license or a request to PitchBook.

name: NotebookLM
blocker: Every user needs a paid Gemini Notebook Enterprise license (subscription of at least 15 licenses). Developers get only a 14-day free trial. The API is a Preview (v1alpha) that requires user-account credentials, and service-account support is unconfirmed.

name: Otter AI
blocker: Core public REST API is gated to the Otter Enterprise plan (may need account manager to enable). The OAuth MCP server is available more broadly but is limited to meeting search/retrieval.

name: higgsfield
blocker: The API has no documented free tier or trial. A developer must fund a pay-as-you-go balance (credits expire after a year) before generating. The account-based MCP/CLI needs a paid subscription. No sales contact is needed for standard use.

name: Mermaid CLI
blocker: It is only a local CLI with narrow scope (render diagrams to files). It has no remote or hosted API and needs Node.js and headless Chromium at runtime, so it could only work as a sandboxed local-execution tool.
